name: Memphis Grizzlies
headline: The Grizzlies started 6-0 against the regular-season slate but have now dropped three straight, including a 128-97 loss to OKC.
good: Memphis is 6-3 with a +6.1 net margin: 117.9 points per game scored against 111.8 allowed, with a 113.4 offensive rating and 107.5 defensive rating.
Ty Jerome is carrying the offense at 26.6 points and 5.1 assists on 62.9 percent true shooting, with a 32.5 percent usage rate.
Cedric Coward is efficient and active: 13.5 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.6 steals, 48.8 percent from three, and a team-best plus-77 total plus/minus.
Rookie Cameron Boozer averages 15.8 points, 10.0 rebounds and 5.2 assists, and the team shoots 37.9 percent from three and 83.9 percent from the line.
bad: The three-game skid: a 134-135 loss to New Orleans, a 103-107 home loss to Indiana, then the 97-128 blowout by Oklahoma City on Friday (Ajay Mitchell had a career-high 35).
Boozer is shooting only 34.7 percent from the field (50.1 percent true shooting) with 3.0 turnovers per game, and the team turns it over 15.8 times a night versus 14.2 for opponents.

Memphis gets outrebounded 48.6 to 42.8 on average on the opponent side, wait, no: it grabs 48.6 per game to opponents' 42.8, but it forces fewer steals (6.2 vs 8.2) and blocks (5.0 vs 6.8) than it allows, so the defense creates little havoc.
fans: Before the slide, ESPN's Tim MacMahon called Memphis the most pleasant surprise in the West and compared them to last year's Suns, while noting it is easier to picture this group improving over the next few seasons. The skid has cooled that buzz a bit, and the Oklahoma City result was lopsided. I could not find recent subreddit or beat-writer takes to quote, so the fan mood here is inferred from the ESPN piece only.
outlook: Memphis visits Toronto tonight (tipoff 12:30 AM UTC on Nov 10, about 7:30 PM Central on Nov 9), where DraftKings has the Raptors at -3.5 and our model gives Memphis a 32.4 percent win chance. Toronto is 5-4 with a similar +5.4 point differential, so this is a real chance to stop the slide but not an easy one.
